_about: NestQuest multi-family cost model. 'sourced' values come from data/multifamily_sources.json or cost_sources.json; 'derived' values are simple calculations from sourced numbers; 'assumption' values are NestQuest planning assumptions. All are shown as such in the app.

nahb.cite: NAHB Cost of Constructing a Home-2024: $162 per finished sq ft (single-family; used for attached townhomes, duplexes and fourplexes, which NAHB does not survey separately).

rlb.cite: Rider Levett Bucknall, North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report Q2 2026, 'Multi-Family' $/sq ft of gross floor area: simple mean of the low end across 18 US cities ($250). Big-city data, so likely on the high side for suburban garden apartments.

gc_overhead_pct_nahb.cite: NAHB 2024 sales-price breakdown: builder overhead 5.7% of price vs construction 64.4% -> 0.089 of construction cost. Added to NAHB-based products only (RLB hard costs already include the contractor).

soft_cost_pct_of_hard.cite: Minnesota Housing (2018): soft costs are 17% of total development cost for new construction without tax credits -> 0.17 / 0.83 = 20.5% of hard costs. One state agency's portfolio; no national market-rate figure was found.

surface_cost_per_space.cite: Midpoint of a sourced range: Ventura County (2022) 'as little as $5,000' per space and VTPI (2021) $20,000 per space for a typical residential project.

structured_cost_per_space.cite: WGI 2026 Parking Structure Cost Outlook: national median $33,300 per space (hard cost).

sqft_per_surface_space.cite: VTPI 5.4 Parking Costs (2022): 250-350 sq ft per space including aisles and landscaping; midpoint 300.

vacancy.cite: U.S. Census Bureau Housing Vacancy Survey, Q2 2026: rental vacancy rate 7.3%.

opex_share.cite: National Apartment Association, 'Where Does a Dollar of Rent Go?' (2026, 2024 data): operating costs 27c + property taxes 10c + payroll 7c + capital expenditures 1c = 45c of each rent dollar.

efficiency_cite.cite: Multifamily Executive (2005): apartments average 70-75% net rentable to gross area; NestQuest uses 72.5% for garden apartments, 95% for fourplexes (shared stair) and 100% for townhomes and duplexes (assumptions).

density_cite.cite: JHP Architecture density rules of thumb (Clark County WA plan record, 2024): townhomes 12-18, small walk-up buildings 15-22, garden apartments 18-25 units/acre. NestQuest uses the top of each range as the default limit; duplexes 12 units/acre is an assumption.

zoning_defaults.cite: Typical multi-family setbacks and lot coverage; no height limit is assumed unless you enter one, so stories are not capped. Enter your jurisdiction's rules for accuracy.

_features_note: Amenity costs are NestQuest planning assumptions, scaled by the state factor.
